papers.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

papers.title: Modular Bayesian Foundation Models: Bayesian time series encoders for OOD detection, routing and forecasting
papers.abstract: Industrial systems continuously generate time series that vary in sampling frequency, scale, dynamics, and operating regime. Consequently a single time-series foundation model may not be able to represent all regimes effectively and retraining a large model for every new dataset or regime shift is computationally expensive. Modular foundation models address this issue by reusing specialised encoders trained on diverse datasets and by allowing the expansion of capabilities through the addition of new experts. This approach requires compact experts to minimize storage cost and a proper selection mechanism of experts for unseen data. We propose a modular foundation model framework that combines end-to-end Bayesian encoder training with uncertainty based routing. Using Singular Bayesian Neural Networks (SBNNs), we build a collection of compact Bayesian encoders whose epistemic uncertainty guides label-free selection. At the selected ranks, our Bayesian collection uses 63.8\% less storage than its deterministic counterpart. We evaluate this framework on time-series data through distribution shift, encoder selection, and probabilistic forecasting. Across seven incoming datasets, uncertainty-based routing is competitive with distance-based routing in terms of forecast MSE, while reducing average ECE from 0.086 to 0.072 and average NLL from 0.907 to 0.836. It also increases PICP90 from 82.28\% to 89.03\%. In a separate model-family comparison, we evaluate the SBNN pipeline against full-rank Bayes by Backprop, deep ensembles, and MC Dropout. The SBNN pipeline achieves an average MSE of 0.390, comparable with 0.396 for deep ensembles, 0.389 for MC dropout, and 0.443 for the full-rank Bayesian model. It uses 63.9\% fewer parameters than MC dropout, 81.9\% fewer than the full-rank model, and 92.8\% fewer than the deep ensemble.

papers.title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics
papers.abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces the number of acquired projections, but conventional sampling strategies are designed primarily for image reconstruction rather than for downstream physical inference. Here, we investigate optimal task-aware projection selection for directly predicting hemodynamics from sparse CT angiography (CTA) measurements. Using computational fluid dynamics simulations of intracranial aneurysms, we generate synthetic fan-beam CTA projections and train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) to predict two targets: the spatially resolved time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS) field and the spatially averaged TAWSS. The FNO was coupled with optimal input selection for simultaneous optimal sampling and training. Our goal was to investigate if agentic AI could discover optimal sampling strategies that outperform current methods. We compared fixed uniform and golden-angle sampling with three task-aware optimal selection strategies: Gumbel-Softmax, a Soft top-K method, and an agentic AI selector. The methods were compared at different view selection budgets. A detailed analysis of the AI agent was performed to understand its reasoning and performance. For spatially resolved TAWSS, Agentic and Soft top-K achieve the lowest mean errors (Agentic performs slightly better) and substantially outperform fixed sampling under extreme sparsity. For spatially averaged TAWSS, optimized selection becomes important at extremely sparse acquisitions. Analysis of the selected masks reveals multiple distinct subsets concentrated around informative regions. Moreover, masks optimized for hemodynamic prediction yield poor image reconstructions, showing that task-optimal acquisition differs fundamentally from reconstruction-optimal acquisition. This work suggests the possibility of designing sparse acquisitions directly around downstream physical quantities.

papers.title: Context Compaction for World Models
papers.abstract: World models let observers explore and interact with generated worlds. Recent work shows that when observers revisit a region, current models often fail to regenerate it consistently. We view this as a context retrieval problem. LLM agents manage context retrieval at two layers of their stack. At the model layer, the KV cache design determines how much context fits in memory. At the agent harness layer, harnesses such as Claude Code pick the context sent to the LLM. Prior work on world models has mostly focused only on the model layer. In this paper, we make three contributions. First, we build a benchmark to measure world model context retrieval. It generates new worlds for every episode, preventing a model from recalling rooms using training data. It also separates context retrieval from guesses based on nearby frames. Second, we build an agent harness that performs context compaction for world models, which to our knowledge no prior work has studied. Third, we use our benchmark to study four world model designs. Context compaction lets our world models retrieve rooms up to 4 times beyond their context window without retraining. However, world models with sliding-window attention lose most of their context retrieval when dreaming. Therefore, a dreaming world agent benefits more from extending the reach of its world model using context compaction than switching to sliding window attention at the model layer.

papers.title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
papers.abstract: The continuous development of machine learning inter-atomic potentials (MLIAPs)has greatly accelerated materials research in recent years. However, the need to con- struct custom MLIAPs for each unique problem remains a bottleneck which raises the question of the transferability of MLIAPs. While foundation MLIAPs can achieve transferability due to the broad coverage of chemical space represented in their training sets, their size and computational cost limits their routine use. We address this gap by developing a lightweight general-purpose MLIAP for metal alloys spanning twelve elements (Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, W). Here, we utilize a step-wise active learning (AL) approach to develop a compact yet diverse dataset and model that generalizes well by interpolating from previously seen interactions. The resulting potentials transfer effectively to unseen, higher body-order alloys systems, requiring only unary and binary training data to capture ternary and quaternary systems. The model also transfers well to new elements via an alchemical extrapolation within the network, requiring only unary data for the new element and its alloys. These findings suggest that MLIAPs trained on targeted, diversity-driven datasets provide transferability at a relatively low computational cost, offering a practical path toward general-purpose, resource-efficient MLIAPs for materials modeling.

papers.title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.

papers.title: Value Function-Guided MPPI for Hierarchical Planning and Control in Off-Road Autonomous Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous navigation in off-road terrain is commonly achieved using hierarchical control and planning architectures that rely on explicit cost maps and one-way information flow from a high-level planner to a low-level controller, decoupling planning from the true execution cost experienced during control. We propose a hierarchical planning and control framework in which information flows bidirectionally, allowing the low-level controller to guide trajectory selection at the planning level. The highest level of the hierarchy is a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control-style planner that determines optimal trajectories and passes these waypoints to a pretrained low-level reinforcement learning (RL) controller. Rather than drawing from an explicit cost map, our MPPI planner leverages the value function of the RL controller as an implicit cost representation. In this formulation, MPPI serves as a trajectory exploration mechanism, while the low-level controller's value function guides the search. To account for the distribution shift seen by the value function between training and evaluation, we propose an online policy evaluation process that adapts the value function to unseen driving experiences, and we demonstrate this adaptation in unseen off-road simulation environments. We evaluate our approach in a high-fidelity off-road driving simulator across a range of challenging terrain conditions and compare its performance against a baseline MPPI controller. The results demonstrate that our method achieves safer and more effective navigation to goal locations while eliminating the need for explicit cost maps and enabling tighter coupling between planning and control.

papers.abstract: Future planetary rovers will traverse steep, deformable terrain where slip, sinkage, and terrain deformation can threaten mobility. Although simulation can capture some wheel-soil effects, unmodeled deformable-terrain phenomena create sim-to-real gaps requiring deployment-time adaptation. Yet, rover operations leave little room for extensive trial-and-error. We introduce TERRA (Targeted Exploration for Reward-Relevant Adaptation), an online adaptation framework that efficiently seeks deployment data exposing task-relevant model errors and corrects them. TERRA adapts a simulation-trained world model with a reward-weighted prediction loss and trains a loss predictor to estimate where future performance-relevant errors are likely to occur, using this signal to guide exploration during MPC. In simulation, TERRA reaches approximately 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe out-of-distribution pretraining conditions, outperforming exploration baselines in reward, completion time, and energy to first success. On the ERNEST rover, TERRA recovers coordinated active-suspension locomotion on a deformable Mars-simulant slope within three to five real-world trials. The method is assessed on the constrained 14-dimensional hydrodynamic optimization of the DTMB 5415 hull under a deliberately limited computational budget. MF-CAS achieves an approximately 9.0% resistance reduction, compared with 6.7% for the best baseline optimisation method, demonstrating that incorporating fidelity-resolved uncertainty directly into the joint location-fidelity decision can substantially improve multifidelity active learning efficiency.

papers.title: A Multi-Layer Navigation System for Smart Wheelchairs with a Limited Input Interface
papers.abstract: Smart wheelchairs are robotic devices that gather information from the surroundings and allow people to safely drive through various environments. They usually rely on the interpretation of high-level user's intentions, typically decoded through human-robot interface (HRI) or brain-machine interface (BMI). However, navigating in an unknown environment and accurately understanding user commands remain significant challenges. Misinterpretation of commands or the environment can lead to user frustration, distrust of the system, or even unsafe situations. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands. The stack relies on a Virtual Sensors-Driven Potential Fields (ViSPF) method for obstacle detection that accounts for the wheelchair's actual size, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) module for trajectory generation, and an open-vocabulary computer vision algorithm for target identification. Finally, a system based on Priority Queue (PQ) was implemented for target selection. We validated our system on a real smart wheelchair with experiments involving 10 participants without disabilities, including scenarios with faulty input interfaces. The results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our system in real-world environments, proving its potential for practical applications in assistive technologies.

papers.title: An Alignment Benchmark for Enterprise Agents on Era by Eon
papers.abstract: AI agents are widely used in enterprises to access business systems and act on them in pursuit of a goal. However, fulfilling a user's request can cause harm. Era by Eon is a product that creates a digital twin of a company by simulating its business systems and data. Its simulators implement the programming interfaces of real products. Our benchmark uses ten of these systems, including Salesforce, Zendesk, Jira and Slack. We tested whether agents would carry out harmful business requests or trust misleading information in company records. We ran 19 models on 41 tasks three times, for 2,337 runs. Of the 2,304 runs that produced an answer, 918 (40%) contained a violation. The most common were false claims about actions or records (290 runs), following planted instructions (266) and disclosing sensitive data to the wrong audience (249). Every attempted change was recorded and blocked before it took effect. Misleading Slack messages caused 16 models to report an incorrect ticket status in 47 of 57 runs. No model was free of violations. The four best models violated in 22 to 24% of their runs. Yet one of them, Nova Pro, did the task correctly in only 30 runs.

papers.title: Force-Driven Hook Disassembly via Constraint-Aware Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The growing volume of end-of-life products has intensified the need for automated disassembly, yet hook-type connections remain challengin: their orientations vary, they deform under load, and their geometry is hidden, so vision alone cannot identify a feasible non-destructive disassembly direction. This work proposes a constraint-aware reinforcement learning framework that infers feasible extraction directions online from contact forces. The policy is trained in a robot-agnostic, object-centric simulation on a simplified peg-in-hole pair and deployed zero-shot on a physical robot, where it transfers to real connections with unseen, multi-stage constraint structures. Because instantaneous contact forces are noisy and locally ambiguous, the policy is coupled with a particle filter belief that provides the policy with temporally integrated directional information and reduces redundant exploratory motion. The approach is validated on four real-world tasks, from peg-in-hole pairs to the inner propeller and front cover of an end-of-life air-conditioning unit. The full method achieves success rates of 100%, 100%, 90%, and 75% with the highest path efficiency on every task, and raises the success rate on the air-conditioning cover from 45% to 75% relative to a policy trained without the belief. These results indicate that force-driven reinforcement learning can enable disassembly without product-specific models or demonstrations.

papers.title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
papers.abstract: Search-based machine-learning (ML) agents improve a solution by writing candidate programs, executing them, and keeping the best. Execution gives the search reliable feedback, but a single run can take hours, and most runs end in programs the agent discards. Recent agents try to save these runs by letting a large language model act as a world model that predicts how each program would perform. However, a wrong prediction feeds the search false information. We argue that an agent does not need to predict the outcome of execution, only the decision that execution would support. We propose World Reward Models (WRMs), which learn from real execution results to choose directly which candidate will perform better, without predicting any intermediate outcome. We prove that a selector which predicts execution from the same inputs cannot outperform the best direct selector, that predicted outcomes add an error which can make a likelihood-trained world model prefer the worse program on every instance, and that cross-entropy on executed winners drives a WRM toward the optimum. Our WRM, ForeCritic, adapts a 9B typed decision model to 5k executed program pairs. On 12,438 held-out pairs from 26 ML tasks, it picks the better program 79.4% of the time, while general-purpose LLM judges reach 53--62%, and its probabilities are calibrated. Inside AIDE, ML-Master, and ForeAgent, it cuts mean task time by 4.4--7.5 times while keeping their mean scores within 0.01 or raising them.

papers.title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics
papers.abstract: Pneumonia changes across respiration, inflammation, and organ function, while the measurements that describe it arrive at different times and are often incomplete. History-aware filtering separates state propagation from observation-driven correction, so a measurement updates the shared belief only when it is observed. That belief supports recursive forecasts of clinical values and modality representations, and summaries of future prognosis. Cap-MBRL searches imagined continuations inside an authorized action set and replaces a frozen fallback only when a candidate meets the risk budget and a predicted-cost margin. On the pneumonia cohort MASS, recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models, and simulated future states retain prognostic information. Trained separately on public MIMIC-IV-CXR chest radiographs and clinical trajectories, this model improves prognostic discrimination over latest-value fusion in development and is competitive on long-horizon error on the locked pneumonia panel. In five known-mechanism MASS-Syn environments, Cap-MBRL lowers selection regret relative to direct fallback execution.

papers.title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
papers.abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

papers.title: Variational Consequence-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) typically mitigates distribution shift by imposing divergence constraints on the action distributions of the learned and behavior policies. However, this paradigm cannot ensure the underlying dynamic consistency structure: even minor action deviations can lead to drastically different transitions, inadvertently driving the agent away from the offline dataset. To address this, we explore policy constraints through their induced state-consequence distributions rather than relying on pure action-distribution matching. Nevertheless, directly enforcing such consequence-aware constraints is computationally intractable without access to the true underlying dynamics model. To bypass this issue, we propose Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR), which replaces the intractable objective with a closed-form latent divergence. Structuring this latent space to reflect transition dynamics renders the latent divergence a theoretically bounded surrogate for the true consequence-distribution divergence. By regularizing the learned policy with this latent divergence, StBR adaptively tightens the behavior constraint in dynamics-sensitive regions, effectively preventing deviations outside the offline dataset. Empirically, we demonstrate that StBR achieves superior performance across diverse offline RL benchmarks.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
papers.abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Matérn/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

papers.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
papers.abstract: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

papers.title: Multiscale topology optimization and experimental testing of metal lattice bridges produced by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: This work explores the synergy between metal additive manufacturing and topology optimization to enable lightweight structures with superior mechanical properties. The study first proposes a novel multi-scale topology optimization methodology to generate lattice-embedded structures, and applies it to the design of a bridge-like part under three-point bending. Four designs are generated, spanning macroscale volume fractions from 15% to 30% to explore mass–stiffness trade-offs. Each design is manufactured four times in a high strength aluminum alloy using laser powder bed fusion. Although pragmatic industrial examples exist, to the authors’ knowledge, this is the first reported study in which topology-optimized, lattice-embedded metal structures were successfully fabricated. Experimental three-point bending tests assess printing quality, the force–displacement response (linear and nonlinear) and failure behavior. The results show excellent print fidelity, low variability, and close agreement between measured and numerical volume fractions. While linear stiffness does not match numerical predictions, the experiments reveal highly tunable crack propagation. In particular, the sequential failure of unit cells leads to stable energy absorption and placement of solid regions is shown to cause direction-changing crack paths. The findings highlight the potential of jointly optimizing lattice geometry and solid–lattice distribution to tailor mechanical response and failure modes in additively manufactured structures.

The major shortcoming of current machine learning and deep learning detectors is that they do not analyze network traffic bidirectionally and prioritize the most indicative attack signatures, resulting in suboptimal detection of stealthy threats. papers.title: Advances in materials for fog harvesting: A comprehensive review of conventional, bioinspired, and advanced functional materials

efficient water harvesting requires a balance between capture, droplet mobility, coalescence, shedding, drainage, mechanical stability, environmental durability, and manufacturability.The review identifies the transition from passive interception-based meshes toward multifunctional, surface-engineered, and bioinspired materials as a major technological development in fog harvesting.

papers.title: Data-driven valorization of mixed olefins byproducts via self-stabilized precipitation polymerization
papers.abstract: The transition of fossil fuels from energy sources to chemical feedstocks has generated huge amount of mixed olefins byproducts, whose efficient valorization remains an important challenge in chemical engineering. Self-stabilized precipitation (2SP) polymerization offers a promising route to directly convert these under-utilized olefins into polymer products without costly separation or other pre-treatments. However, the multi-factor nature of 2SP leaves its mechanism largely speculative, and the reaction feasibility currently relies on time-consuming trial-and-error experimentation. Here, we developed a machine learning predictor, 2SP-MLP, trained on 844 experimental data points to enable rapid and accurate prediction of 2SP outcomes. Following Bayesian optimization with 5-fold cross-validation, the XGBoost classifier achieved the best performance (ACC = 0.90, AUC = 0.96). Interpretability analysis identified the monomer-solvent solubility parameter difference (exceeding 3.6 MPa 1/2 ) as the key factor governing precipitation feasibility. Beyond solubility parameter, mechanistic analyses suggested that molecular shape, flexibility and charge distribution influenced polymer precipitation and microparticle formation (for polymer precipitation, ACC = 0.94 and AUC = 0.97; for microparticle formation, ACC = 0.67 and AUC = 0.71). Regression models for particle yield and olefin conversion both performed best with XGBoost (R 2 = 0.73 and 0.89, respectively). Experimental validation on 10 untested formulations with different monomer combinations, feed ratios, and solvent types achieved 70% prediction accuracy, especially on FT mixed olefins-related systems. Overall, this work provides a data-driven tool that accelerates process design and reduces experimental cost for 2SP-based valorization of mixed olefins, demonstrating the potential of ML to advance sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: CP-BayesNE: Uncertainty-Aware Personalized Nutrient-Density Estimation from Food Images Using Conformal Prediction and Prior-Corrected Dietary Adaptation
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable longitudinal dietary assessment is a prerequisite for precision nutrition, important for studying nutrition-related changes in health and physical function, but conventional dietary recording can impose substantial user burden. AI-driven, food-image-based assessment can reduce this burden, although uncertainty in food recognition and inter-individual dietary differences may propagate to nutrient estimation. Methods:We developed CP-BayesNE, an uncertainty-aware framework that combines temperature-scaled food classification, conformal candidate sets, training-prior-corrected dietary-history personalization, and posterior-weighted nutrient estimation to support AI-driven personalized nutrition. Results: EfficientNetV2-S achieved 78.01% Top-1 and 93.67% Top-5 accuracy, while temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.11238 to 0.04345. At α=0.10, regularized adaptive prediction sets reduced the average candidate-set size from 80.78 to 5.77 while maintaining 94.32% empirical category coverage. In FoodLogAthl-218, prior-corrected personalization reduced nutrient density mean absolute error (MAE) by 4.0–6.6% across energy and macronutrients over 51 users. A single-participant 92-meal personal dataset provided preliminary end-to-end feasibility evidence, while also revealing limitations, including slightly worse fat MAE and conservative nutrient intervals. Conclusions: These findings support uncertainty-aware personalized dietary assessment while emphasizing that category-level conformal validity does not directly imply accurate true dietary intake.

papers.title: A physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin for personalized estimation of arterial stiffness
papers.abstract: Abstract Arterial stiffness, commonly assessed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), is an important biomarker of cardiovascular risk, yet conventional PWV measurements require dual-site recordings that limit scalability in clinical settings. Here we introduce a physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin framework for estimating central-brachial arterial stiffness from a single brachial pressure waveform. Using our laboratory-developed cuff device, high-resolution brachial pulse waveforms were collected in a cohort of 118 subjects. The digital twin then personalizes a reduced-order wave propagation model through PDE-constrained optimization, generating a compact parameter space that encodes ventricular–vascular characteristics relevant to stiffness. Incorporating digital-twin-derived parameters improved PWV estimation on a blind test cohort ( r = 0.67, RMSE = 1.12 m/s) compared with a baseline model using only age and blood pressure ( r = 0.22, RMSE = 1.90 m/s). These results indicate that physics-informed digital twins can enable scalable, noninvasive assessment of vascular aging from accessible peripheral waveforms.

papers.title: Causal Digital Twin-Enabled Deep Reinforcement Learning for Energy-Efficient and Explainable Resource Allocation in 6G Networks
papers.abstract: The proliferation of sixth-generation (6G) networks has intensified the need for intelligent resource allocation strategies that simultaneously satisfy stringent quality-of-service requirements and minimize energy consumption. However, conventional deep reinforcement learning approaches often suffer from poor generalization under distribution shifts and provide limited explainability regarding their decision-making processes. We propose a Causal Digital Twin framework that constructs a structural virtual replica of the physical 6G network by encoding causal dependencies among base stations, user equipment, and edge servers through a causal graph neural network. This twin captures the underlying causal mechanisms governing network behavior rather than merely fitting statistical correlations. Furthermore, invariant risk minimization and disentangled representation learning are employed to ensure that the learned representations remain stable across diverse traffic regimes, hence improving robustness under varying operational conditions. The resulting differentiable simulator enables gradient-based actor-critic optimization within a constrained Markov decision process formulation, where energy efficiency is maximized subject to latency and rate constraints. Counterfactual rollouts are then generated to assess the causal impact of specific allocation decisions, thereby providing explainability and facilitating sim-to-real transfer. The proposed method is expected to achieve substantial energy savings while maintaining service reliability, and the causal structure of the digital twin offers interpretable insights into the factors driving each decision.

papers.abstract: Large bone defects require scaffolds that combine mechanical support, biological activity, and anatomical adaptability.Metamaterials use deliberately designed structure to control effective properties beyond bulk composition.This narrative review examines metallic, ceramic, bioglass, polymeric, and composite metamaterial platforms for bone repair.It then considers mechanical, electroactive, magnetic, ultrasoundresponsive, photoresponsive, thermoresponsive, and shape-memory strategies.These structures can regulate modulus, stress transfer, pore connectivity, mass transport, degradation, and local stimulus delivery.The resulting local conditions influence bone ingrowth, vascularization, osteoimmune transitions, infection control, post-tumor reconstruction, and osseointegration.At the cell-material interface, structural and physical influence engage YAP/TAZ, integrin/FAK, Wnt/β-catenin, HIF-1α/VEGF, BMP/Smad, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, and MAPK signaling.Translation remains constrained by limited fatigue data, poorly resolved in vivo pathway crosstalk, manufacturing variability, and excessive system complexity.Future designs should match a defined clinical indication and prioritize scalable fabrication, predictable mechanical and degradation behavior, long-term remodeling, and clinically relevant validation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in gut-brain axis research for Alzheimer’s disease: From associative insights toward causal inference and personalized interventions
papers.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research is shifting from a “brain-centered” model toward a “gut-brain axis system” perspective. However, the causal roles of gut microbiota in AD pathology remain elusive, as traditional association studies struggle to distinguish potential drivers from passengers. This review examines the potential applications and inherent limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) in dissecting this complex relationship. We discuss three emerging and conceptually promising directions: First, AI-frameworks for hypothesis-generating causal discovery that can prioritize microbiota-AD relationships for subsequent experimental validation, while recognizing that current approaches predominantly identify statistical associations rather than empirically supported causal conclusions; second, multi-modal fusion networks, when applied with appropriate regularization and validation, can assist in constructing cross-scale molecular maps across microbiota, metabolites, and the brain, though such pathway inferences require careful interpretation as they represent statistical associations rather than biochemically validated mechanisms; and third, the conceptual application of digital twin-based simulation as a long-term vision for personalized microbiota modulation, which currently lacks the ecological resolution and validation required for predictive modeling. By integrating multi-pathway mechanisms of the gut-brain axis and characteristic profiles of gut microbiota, we critically evaluate the technical advantages of machine learning in microbiome data analysis alongside major challenges including overfitting, batch effects, confounding factors, and reproducibility. Leveraging AI-driven microbiota analysis, we propose a phased translational roadmap, from near-term standardization and cross-cohort validation, through mid-term endophenotyping and trial enrichment strategies, to the long-term exploration of personalized interventions, toward the eventual goal of precision prevention. This article outlines a full-cycle framework from discovery to clinical translation and envisions a conceptual ecosystem for future intelligent microecological health management. Achieving the promise of AI-empowered gut-brain axis research will require deep integration across neuroscience, microbiology, computational science, and clinical medicine, alongside rigorous experimental validation, standardized protocols, and realistic appraisal of current technological boundaries.

papers.title: Mechanical Degradation and Fracture Behavior of PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V Induced by Rubber-Glove Contamination
papers.abstract: This study quantifies the mechanical degradation caused by locally introduced rubber-glove contamination in stress-relieved PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V. Rubber-glove fragments were inserted into defined build layers of standardized tensile specimens and into highly loaded transition regions of a topology-optimized bracket demonstrator. Twelve uncontaminated and twelve contaminated tensile specimens and nine brackets per condition were evaluated. The contaminated tensile specimens exhibited a mean ultimate strength of approx. 860 MPa compared with approx. 1200 MPa for the reference condition, corresponding to a reduction of approx. 28%. Mean elongation at break decreased from approx. 13.4% to 0.6%, representing a reduction of approx. 95%. Fracture preferentially occurred at the contamination insertion region and was associated with planar fracture features and retained spherical powder particles. The results support a predominantly defect-controlled degradation mechanism associated with locally disturbed consolidation.

papers.title: Next-Generation Zero-Server Edge Electronic Design Automation
papers.abstract: Abstract Circuit simulation in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) must balance circuit models, numerical meth- ods, and hardware resources. Traditional SPICE- like tools assemble circuit equations using Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA), then obtain numerical so- lutions through nonlinear iteration, transient inte- gration, and sparse matrix solvers. Their strengths are mature models and traceable results; their costs are the memory and computation time required by large netlists. The basic idea of Edge Web EDA is to let users launch interactive circuit analysis in a browser and delegate part of the computation to WebAssembly and WebGPU. This direction is technically plausible: WebAssembly provides a portable execution envi- ronment near native performance, WebGPU pro- vides general-purpose compute shaders, and regu- lar operations such as sparse matrix-vector multi- plication have parallelization potential. However, the WebGPU core does not provide ready-made CSR, CG, LU, or SPICE solvers; nor can WGSL currently be treated as a universally available native double- precision environment [12, 13]. The main conclusion is that Edge Web EDA is suitable as an auxiliary layer for early design ex- ploration, parameter sweeps, teaching, and real- time visualization. It should not claim to re- place transient SPICE or tape-out sign-off compre- hensively without reproducible benchmarks, inde- pendent high-precision reference solutions, real- istic process models, and measurement compar- isons. Mixed-precision iterative refinement, PINNs, and FNOs may all provide speed advantages within clearly defined validation domains, but their cor- rectness and generalization must be assessed jointly using condition numbers, residuals, forward error, unseen topologies, and extreme operating condi- tions. This monograph also argues that “zero-server” should not mean that no backend or infrastructure exists at all. It should mean that, in a specified op- erating mode, the principal data and computation can remain on the user’s device. Sensitive PDKs, complete sign-off, and large simulations may still re- quire controlled servers or a cloud-edge collabora- tion architecture. papers.title: Perceptions and experiences of learning through concept mapping among undergraduate optometry students
papers.abstract: Clinical Relevance Concept mapping (CM), as an educational tool that facilitates meaningful learning, can help eye care professionals develop clinical reasoning and effectively integrate cognitive skills into clinical practice.Background Concept mapping (CM) is an active learning tool that fosters critical thinking and clinical reasoning. Despite its potential benefits in learning, the use of CM remains underutilised in optometry education. This study aims to compare the learning experiences of undergraduate optometry students at LV Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI), India, and the University of New South Wales (UNSW), Sydney, on CM.Methods This prospective study had three phases. In the pre-class phase, students received pre-reading materials. In the second phase, they participated in collaborative CM-building activities in small groups, followed by individual CM construction. In the final phase, students completed an online survey assessing their familiarity with CM, perceived benefits, challenges, and overall learning experience.Results A total of 29 LVPEI and 36 UNSW students completed the survey. A higher percentage of UNSW students reported prior familiarity with CM compared to LVPEI students (39% vs. 14% at LVPEI, p = 0.025). The majority of students from both LVPEI (61%) and UNSW (81%, p = 0.25) related new information to previous knowledge and agreed that CM encouraged critical thinking (LVPEI 83% vs. UNSW 81%, p = 0.82). Identifying concepts was certainly or somewhat a challenge for LVPEI compared to UNSW students (93% vs. 42%, p < 0.001), while linking concepts was somewhat a challenge for both groups (LVPEI 58%, UNSW 57%, p = 0.05). A positive overall experience was reported by 83% at LVPEI and 97% at UNSW.Conclusion Integrating CM into optometry education had a positive impact on student learning experiences. Despite challenges, students from both institutions acknowledged its benefits, highlighting its potential as an effective learning strategy in optometry education.

papers.title: Influence maximization in twitter mention networks: a comparative analysis of PageRank and out-degree heuristics under the Independent Cascade model
papers.abstract: Identifying structurally prominent users and selecting effective seed nodes are central problems in social network analysis and influence maximization. This study analyzes a directed Twitter mention network constructed from approximately 1.6 million tweets, comprising 552,121 users and 641,497 directed edges. We characterize user positions using PageRank, in-degree, and out-degree centrality and compare PageRank-based and out-degree-based seed selection under the Independent Cascade (IC) model. The network exhibits highly skewed structural centrality patterns. Seed-set performance is evaluated through 1,000 independent Monte Carlo simulations with a uniform propagation probability of \(p=0.1\) . We report mean spread, standard deviation, 95% confidence intervals, minimum and maximum spread, and zero-additional-activation frequency. Under the adopted graph representation and IC assumptions, the out-degree-based seed set achieves a substantially larger simulated spread than the PageRank-based seed set. This difference is consistent with the diffusion mechanism because activation attempts follow outgoing mention edges, giving high-out-degree nodes more immediate opportunities to propagate. These findings are conditional on the constructed mention graph and the uniform-probability IC model. A mention edge does not necessarily represent the direction of real-world social influence, and the simulations do not incorporate temporal dynamics, content-specific effects, or empirically estimated propagation probabilities. Therefore, the results should not be interpreted as evidence that either heuristic is universally superior for real-world influence maximization. Overall, the study provides a reproducible structural and simulation-based comparison of two seed-selection heuristics while emphasizing the importance of edge interpretation, diffusion assumptions, uncertainty quantification, and empirical validation.

papers.abstract: Abstract Fused deposition modeling (FDM) of shape-memory polylactic acid (PLA) offers opportunities for thermally responsive architectures, but its brittleness limits structural applications. Here, predominantly bio-based PLA/poly(ethylene furanoate) (PEF) blends were developed using a multifunctional epoxy-based chain extender (ADR) for reactive compatibilization. Molecular dynamics simulations and scanning electron microscopy indicated limited thermodynamic compatibility and interfacial defects in uncompatibilized blends. Adding 0.1–0.3 wt % ADR to a PLA/PEF blend with polymer mass ration of 90/10 refined the dispersed morphology and increased low-frequency melt elasticity, consistent with improved interfacial coupling. The characteristic PEF-domain diameter decreased from 0.55 to 0.20 μm. The blend containing 0.1 wt % ADR produced an elongation at break of 10.8%. ADR increase the shape recovery ratio of bent specimens from 73.7% to 87.0%. Gyroid and Diamond triply periodic minimal surface architectures printed from the blend containing 0.1 wt % ADR exhibited sustained compressive load-bearing behavior and recovery ratios of 92.13% and 89.25%, respectively. These findings demonstrate a predominantly bio-based material approach for recoverable 4D-printed architectures, which highlight the potential in thermally-responsive engineering architectures including deployable energy absorbers and biomedical components.

papers.title: A Nonlinear Model Predictive Control framework for TEC-based BTMS in Light Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: This paper presents a Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NLMPC) strategy for the energy-efficient thermal management of Light Electric Vehicle (LEV) batteries using Thermoelectric Coolers (TECs). While LEVs feature compact battery packs with small thermal masses, TECs provide a solid-state, space-efficient cooling solution ideal for this platform. However, TECs act as a parasitic load, drawing energy from the battery and increasing internal heat generation. While linear Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategies have been considered, their reliance on a model linearized around a specific operating point renders them inadequate for the strong, non-linear dynamics of a TEC-BTMS. A full NLMPC strategy, despite its theoretical superiority, has not yet been applied to this problem. Furthermore, existing controllers ignore the parasitic load of TECs, which draws energy from the battery, thereby increasing the heat generation. To address this, the NLMPC’s internal model is developed to explicitly couple the TEC’s parasitic load with the battery’s heat generation. Simulations show that the NLMPC controller provides a 47.3% to 74.2% reduction in energy usage compared to a relay controller across all tested conditions. Compared to the Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller tuned at an ambient temperature of 25 °C, the NLMPC provides similar energy consumption while at higher ambient temperatures it saves up to 51.8% energy. The novel parasitic load coupling of TECs within the NLMPC accounts for up to 25% energy saving from baseline NLMPC. The results demonstrate that NLMPC significantly enhances both thermal management and energy efficiency, addressing key challenges in LEV battery systems and extending vehicle range.

papers.title: Dynamics of waste discharge pollutant concentration and heat source/sink effects across a nonlinear stretching surface conveying tri-hybrid nanofluids: a multi-output MLP-ANN surrogate approach
papers.abstract: The analysis of nanofluid circulation over a nonlinear stretching surface plays an important role in areas such as thermal engineering, pollutant control systems, polymer processing, coating technology, cooling equipment, and advanced manufacturing processes. Motivated by the above applications, the present study investigates the combined effects of heat source/sink, porous medium, activation energy, pollutant discharge concentration, velocity slip, and thermal slip effects of a tri-hybrid nanofluid flow over a nonlinear stretching surface. The governing flow equations are converted into a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations and solved computationally with the help of the RKF-45 algorithm together with a shooting procedure. A multi-output multilayer perceptron artificial neural network is subsequently developed as a data-driven surrogate for the simultaneous prediction of engineering factors. The proposed model achieved a mean testing normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 1.0705 × 10 − 6 and a mean testing mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.2560 × 10 − 4 %. Comparative evaluation against radial basis function neural network (RBFNN), Gaussian support vector regression (SVR), sparse Gaussian process regression (GPR), and LSBoost models demonstrated that the multi-output multi-layer perceptron artificial neural network (MO-MLP-ANN) provided the lowest testing error within the examined one-at-a-time sampled domain.

papers.title: CauCity-WM: an intervention-consistent generative world model for counterfactual urban dynamics and risk-aware decision making
papers.abstract: Urban decision making requires more than accurate forecasting: it requires estimating how the same realized episode would evolve under an action that was not taken. We introduce CauCity-WM, an intervention-consistent generative world model whose methodological core is a noise-preserving twin-world transition. The model abducts an episode-specific structural disturbance from the factual trajectory and then reuses both that disturbance and the same diffusion base-noise path in factual and counterfactual rollouts, changing only the intervention. This defines a unit-level counterfactual semantics for a graph-conditioned diffusion world model rather than treating causality as an auxiliary prediction head. Mechanism-gradient alignment promotes transfer across cities and regimes, sparse intervention Jacobians constrain action propagation, and risk-sensitive planning optimizes CVaR-regularized actions through the same transition law. Across seven real urban forecasting benchmarks, CauCity-WMreduces average MAE relative to the strongest forecasting baseline. In counterfactual evaluation, it achieves an E-MAE of 2.61 and PEHE of 3.29, compared with 3.22 and 4.07 for the strongest adapted causal baseline, while attaining 84.6% effect-sign accuracy and 89.6% coverage of nominal 90% effect intervals. In calibrated SUMO scenarios, it reduces mean travel time to 27.1 min and constraint violations to 1.9%. These results support intervention-consistent urban world modeling as a practical basis for counterfactual analysis and risk-aware decision making. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CauCity_WM-C563 .

papers.title: Physics informed neural network surrogate modeling and global sensitivity analysis of magnetized nanofluid flow over a porous cylinder for solar thermal energy applications
papers.abstract: Abstract The accurate prediction of mass and heat transfer dynamics in the movement of magnetized nanofluids over porous cylindrical structures is crucial for the design and improvement of innovative solar thermal energy systems. However, traditional numerical methods need comprehensive high-fidelity simulations over several parameter domains, limiting their use in real-time evaluation, optimization, and decision-making. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are becoming dependable alternatives to traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods for modeling nonlinear fluid dynamics in aerospace and medical engineering. In this study, we introduced a hybrid framework that leverage PINNs, and an adapted finite difference method to improve the computational analysis of nonlinear magnetized ternary nanofluid flow produced by a permeable stretching cylinder. The investigated working fluid is composed of multi-walled carbon nanotubes, $$A7075$$ A 7075 , and graphene oxide nanoparticles suspended in a blend of ethylene glycol and water.The framework of the PINNs, which includes a defined number of hidden layers, a training algorithm, a learning rate, and an epoch count, has been determined through systematic hyper-parameter optimization. We additionally integrated the dynamic influences of magneto hydrodynamic (MHD) phenomena, activation energy, and thermal radiation to enhance heat transfer and regulate fluid flow phenomena. The established set of mathematical equations are addressed using a modified finite difference method and PINNs to accurately predict fluid flow characteristics. The global sensitivity analysis (GSA) was performed to demonstrate the sensitivity and impact of governing factors on fluid dynamics. Thermal radiation and the Biot number strongly influence temperature variance, while the concentration of nanoparticles acts as a governing factor that exerts significant impacts on velocity and heat transmission. The persistently low PINNs loss metrics, remaining below $${10}^{-11}$$ 10 − 11 , indicate exceptional computational precision and validate the great fidelity of the suggested architecture in accurately representing the controlling thermodynamics of the system. Moreover, the DNN-enforced PINNs approach efficiently corresponds to solutions for an intricate thermal-fluid framework with coefficient of determination $$({R}^{2}\mathrm{) > 0.99}$$ ( R 2 )>0.99 . The established PINN surrogate delivers rapid predictions post-training, significantly alleviating the computing cost linked to recurrent high-fidelity numerical simulations, thus presenting an effective option for parametric analysis and global sensitivity evaluation.

papers.title: Selected topics in quantum scattering theory and emerging optimal-transport methods
papers.abstract: Quantum scattering connects microscopic dynamics to amplitudes, phase shifts, cross sections, transport coefficients, and resonances. This selective Review organizes the Lippmann–Schwinger equation, resolvents, transfer and scattering matrices, nonequilibrium Green’s functions, and R-matrix theory as related representations of a common scattering problem. Born, Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin, and eikonal error tests accompany comparisons of numerical scaling, stability, and method selection. Inverse scattering is examined through the effects of phase loss, incomplete aperture, Jacobian null spaces, singular-value decay, model discrepancy, and noise, together with regularized, Bayesian, and learned approaches for stabilizing reconstruction. The Review then discusses probability-level optimal transport and its extension to emerging amplitude-based formulations, using the Quantum Optimal Transport Amplitude Method (QOTAM) as a concrete example. Its Euclidean and real-time variational constructions are summarized and tested across resonant barriers, multichannel and angular scattering, three-dimensional targets, and disordered waveguides. Independent reference calculations verify complex-amplitude closure, unitarity, flux conservation, and optical-theorem relations to benchmark-dependent numerical precision. In inverse problems, QOTAM is found to be competitive with correctly specified phase-sensitive likelihood methods while showing useful robustness in selected model-mismatch tests. These examples illustrate the promise of optimal-transport-based scattering methods. More broadly, the Review emphasizes how physical constraints, uncertainty quantification, identifiability, and computational scalability jointly shape reliable forward and inverse-scattering analyses.

Phase 2 examined the structural consistency of the model with empirical data. Phase 3 developed a learning ecosystem model to enhance teachers’ active learning in schools under Local Administrative Organizations in Northeastern Thailand. The sample consisted of 550 school administrators and teachers under Local Administrative Organizations in Northeastern Thailand, obtained through multistage random sampling. The research instruments included a rating scale questionnaire with a reliability coefficient of 0.98 and a semi-structured interview. Data were analyzed using Mplus version 8.0 and SPSS version 26 for descriptive statistics and inferential statistics. The findings revealed that: 1) The learning ecosystem comprised five major components and twenty-one subcomponents. Teachers’ active learning consisted of six major components and twenty-two subcomponents, all meeting the prescribed criteria for appropriateness. 2) The structural equation model of the learning ecosystem influencing teachers’ active learning demonstrated a good fit with empirical data, with χ² = 1,103.74, df = 930, χ²/df = 1.187, SRMR = 0.025, RMSEA = 0.018, CFI = 0.996, and TLI = 0.996. 3) The learning ecosystem model for enhancing teachers’ active learning in schools under Local Administrative Organizations in Northeastern Thailand comprised: (1) Preparation and Understanding (Foundation); (2) Building the Learning Ecosystem; (3) Teacher Empowerment; (4) Sustaining Progress; and (5) Impact and Scaling. The model demonstrated the highest levels of suitability, feasibility, and utility.

papers.title: Critical Thinking Disposition among Vietnamese Pharmacy Students:Validation and Predictors
papers.abstract: This study validated the Critical Thinking Disposition Scale (CTDS) and examined predictors of critical thinking among Vietnamese pharmacy students. A cross-sectional study of 833 students used a validated instrument, with Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirming a robust two-factor structure (CFI = 0.968, RMSEA = 0.068). Students showed a moderate overall disposition (M = 33.81, SD = 4.51), with higher Reflective Skepticism than Critical Openness. Bayesian Model Averaging and regression identified fifth-year status and enjoyment of pharmacy studies as statistically significant correlates within the evaluated dataset (R² = 3.91%). Fifth-year students scored significantly higher (p < 0.001), whereas fourth-year students did not differ from third-year students. GPA and gender were not significant predictors. The findings suggested that intensive experiential clinical learning in the final year may foster critical thinking development. Earlier integration of active learning and clinical simulation may help reduce developmental gaps and promote more balanced critical thinking profiles.

papers.title: DETECTING BRAIN TUMORS IN MRI IMAGES USING A HYBRID APPROACH OF MACHINE LEARNING AND BAYESIAN OPTIMIZATION
papers.abstract: One of the most important neurological diseases that demands accurate and timely diagnosis by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is brain tumors. But the manual analysis of MRI images is time-consuming and may be influenced by image characteristics and diagnostic interpretation. In this study, a systematic pixel-based feature extraction method is proposed in combination with a Deep Multi-Layer Perceptron (DMLP), based on Bayesian Optimization (BO), for optimized brain tumor detection without the need for human intervention. The proposed framework involves processing the MRI images to obtain the desired region of interest (ROI) and deriving the required numerical features based on each extracted pixel of the ROI. Bayesian Optimization is used to automate the decision of the number of neurons in the two hidden layers, minimizing the need to design the structure of the network manually. The optimized model in the second phase of the optimization process had 126 neurons in the first hidden layer and 59 neurons in the second hidden layer, with a best model validation performance of 98.54%. With the aid of this optimized architecture, the final model achieved an accuracy of 98.84%, and the precision, recall, and F1-score were 98.84%, 98.82%, and 98.83% on the evaluated test data, respectively, while the specificity was 98.82%. The results have shown that systematic MRI pixel extraction, CAD, DMLP classification, and Bayesian hyperparameter optimization can offer a viable computational framework to automate brain tumor detection.
